title: Prove sharp COPY cost 72 for the A3+D5 decoder (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof with exhaustive finite premises: the fixed A3 weights + D5 root-basis nine-normal decoder proposed by joaqcoo in [#1224](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1224) has exact separate-term COPY optimum **72** on all 120 E8 root lines, allowing arbitrary independent complex row shifts.

```text
source sparsest-row witness and bounded searches: cost 81
new optimum:                                  cost 72
nine-active-term attaining ranks:             (1,8,9,9,9,9,9,9,9)
```

The new lower bound covers every complex shift assignment. The proof reduces it to four complete binary-plane and forced-space certificates. This is a fixed-family result, with no new kappa or supplier admission. Only `research/a3-d5-decoder-floor/` is added. Produced by Nick Petalas.

Credit joaqcoo #1224 for the exact normal frame, normal form and open residual question; Philipp / mightyOil #1248 and Adam Gall #2062 for the deficiency-plane and forced-space methods; DreamingOfClouds #717/#595/#446 for the separate pairing-rank cost model; and the retained E8, eight-term decoder and supplier lineage. The source PR1224 head is `00e6ed0810b8ebc7f6133e2c036d0f1c9a3a4162`. Provenance binds retained source bytes on canonical base `ec2780e8aeb1c88acaf5e9e470ef8c68e7fbbb6c`.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19146053).

## Evidence

Before, the source's fixed A3+D5 example and its three recorded unpunctured searches cost 81. After, an exact all-nine-active witness costs 72, and the exhaustive finite premises prove no allowed shift assignment is cheaper. The source's searches were cited, not rerun.

- All four anchors check 43,435 binary planes each, for 173,740 total. Every partner space has dimension at most one. All 13,812 complete signature/subset cases satisfy the forced-space bound, and all 6,132 literal annihilator computations agree with the compatibility tables.
- Both attaining witnesses pass all 14,400 all-pairs identity entries. Their ranks are computed directly from actual restricted binary pairing matrices. Three altered identities are rejected; a noncritical rational shift remains exact. Each anchor has a case exposing the false bound obtained by discarding a forced constraint.
- Direct warning-strict normal and optimized checks pass locally on CPython 3.12.15, macOS 27.0.1 arm64. They took 1.308 s and 1.298 s, below the 120-second registered limits. These are check durations, not performance comparisons. Their generated five-source-hash receipts agree completely.
- Registered package replay, metadata/pins, exact source-fixture binding, AST/function-size inspection and whitespace checks pass. Every registered local command ran. Committed-byte/source-history preflight passes for all five package files at `703f62bb7da9feed48d9de58e88b73a6ebd7f6c4`.
- Official committed export and export integrity pass. Optimized replay from its read-only Git-free export, with `PATH=/nonexistent`, emits the same receipt and leaves every exported file unchanged. No receipt is handwritten.

Reproduce from the repository root, using this interpreter or another CPython 3.12 installation. Only the standard library is needed.

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/a3-d5-decoder-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/a3-d5-decoder-floor/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/a3-d5-decoder-floor
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/a3-d5-decoder-floor --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_A3_D5_DECODER_FLOOR`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The theorem covers this unpunctured fixed nine-normal frame, all-pairs exactness with ordinary transpose, arbitrary complex row shifts, and separate-term binary pairing-rank billing. Changed frames, punctures, masked-only identities and shared COPY billing are outside scope. The ratio 72/120 equals 3/5, so the optimized family still does not improve the ordinary P120 COPY comparator or supply a complete physical gain.

Source preparation, movement, frame changes, dirty restoration, hosting, precision, stock, compiler and the full consumer invoice remain unknown. No selected operator replay, Lean, Docker, separate static analyzer or complete multiplication theorem is supplied. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. The Python allocation deviation and fixed computation bounds are documented.

The historical card's required orientation command was attempted and fails with `KeyError: complex_profile` because it expects an older selected schema. The current `scripts/research_selected_baseline.py` source-binding orientation passes. Neither is scientific evidence for this result, and this PR does not modify that unrelated helper.

## Open next questions

Can the same A3+D5 family beat the applicable COPY comparator after a specified nontrivial puncture? First derive all nine reader spans and five fixed-term costs for one geometrically justified live set. Those ranks, replacement finite lemmas and the complete physical consumer invoice are missing. The present result does not reserve or investigate that follow-up.

## Related open work

No open PR for the same fixed A3+D5 all-pairs optimum was found in the live publication check. Adjacent decoder COPY work includes:

- [#5064](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5064), head `8ba8ee80081e5efcbaa7245cac230fda2963b14c`: searches changed masked P112/P120 completions and factor bases. This proves a fixed all-pairs family optimum. Its reported P120 cost 72 numerically matches our 72 in a different family; no candidate from that search was replayed here.
- [#5088](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5088), head `ce35592fc32351125435ecfd9f3f809bb898d312`: studies a two-star masked P112 support dictionary and an inconclusive COPY63 search. The live set, support family and claim type differ; no shared optimum is asserted.

Canonical main was fetched again before committing and remains `ec2780e8aeb1c88acaf5e9e470ef8c68e7fbbb6c`, priority revision 7. Live claims, question reservations, open PR bodies, distinctive merged searches and main-tree README searches were refreshed. Sparse local-note coverage is incomplete; search coverage is not a novelty certificate.
